title: chains: default values and nsize cap
purpose: Exercises `chains` [@epsrmanual], which finds chains of bonded molecules with the shortest-path criterion of Franzblau [@franzblau1991] as cited in the Fortran: a bond requires an atom1-atom2 pair in one molecule and atom3 in another within three distance windows (and optionally an atom2-atom1-atom3 angle range); chains start at molecules with one neighbour, and histograms of neighbour numbers and chain lengths are written. This case checks the keyword defaults.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Single criterion S(-O)···S between DMSO molecules: S-O 1.3-1.7 Å within a molecule, S···S 3.5-5.5 Å and O···S 2.5-5.0 Å between molecules; water molecules have no neighbours and count as chains of length 1. Reference `fort.14`: mean neighbour number 0.70, mean chain length 11.1. DMSO has no O-H donor, so this criterion uses S···S proximity to probe the self-association of DMSO in the mixture.
inputs: `ss.CHAINS.dat`: only `fnameato`, `nsize 300` and the criterion. `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test; the keyword file was written by hand (the Fortran program creates no template when the named file does not exist; keywords and defaults from `setup_symbols_generic.f`).
verification: `repeat 2`. `nsize 300` exceeds `mchain` = 200 and is capped; `nsumt`, `ndist` and the angle keywords are not given, so the defaults are used, including the computed `nsize` text "Maximum chain length (max 200)" of `setup_symbols_chains`, visible in the rewritten `.dat` together with `nsize 200`, `ang213max 180.0` and `nsumt -1` (no accumulation). Compared after each pass: `ss.CHAINS.n01`, `ss.CHAINS.dat`, `fort.14`.
